title: Residency audit playback and region-pin assertion workflow
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Compliance customers require deterministic proof that a request honored tenant residency constraints (region pinning + retention rules). Current evidence exports list final routing and storage locations but do not capture the decision path, fallbacks, or the exact telemetry used to make the decision. This makes incident investigations and regulator audits slow and error-prone.

Goal: Ship a 'Residency Audit Playback' feature that records and can replay the decision trail for a hosted API request, and an accompanying 'Pin Assertion' artifact that certifies which region pins were asserted, when overrides occurred, and what fallback policy applied. The playback must be compact, tamper-evident, and exportable as a compliance bundle.

Scope:
- Capture decision telemetry for hosted API requests: routing policy eval, model variant selection, region pin rules, cache hits, and final storage/retention assignment.
- Provide an export format (signed JSON + manifest) suitable for regulator review and internal attestations.
- Console UI: timeline view per-request and an export button on tenant audit pages.
- API: endpoints to fetch playback events and to produce a signed evidence bundle.
- Runtime: lightweight event snapshots stored in a retention-configurable audit store separate from request logs.

Out of scope for initial iteration: live replaying of logic in production path (we will provide read-only playback from stored events), on-prem agent instrumentation changes, and full legal review of evidence format (legal will be engaged for compliance contract language).

Acceptance criteria:
1) For 95% of hosted API requests under test harness, the playback artifact contains the full decision path: inbound header residency assertions, policy rule evaluation, routing choices, fallback triggers, and final region assignment.
2) Console shows a per-request timeline and pin assertions with human-readable reason codes.
3) Exported bundle includes: signed manifest, sequence of timestamped events, relevant configuration snapshots (pinset version + policy hash), and links to storage retention policy.
4) Evidence bundle size stays under 250KB for median request; compresses well for larger payloads.
5) Retrieval latency for playback API <= 300ms for recent requests (30 days).

UX notes:
- Add 'View Residency Playback' action to Tenant -> Activity -> Request Details.
- Timeline has swimlanes: Policy Eval, Routing, Model Variant, Storage/Retention. Each event node expands with small 'why' text and link to the config snapshot.
- Export flow allows 'include configuration snapshots' toggle and TTL for evidence download links.

Telemetry and schema:
- Event envelope fields: request_id, timestamp, actor (router|policy-engine|kv-cache), event_type, reason_code, payload_hash, config_version.
- Store minimal payloads; large items are referenced by object id in the audit store to keep bundle size small.
- Each bundle is signed with platform key (KMS) and contains a content-hash chain to detect tampering.

API endpoints (proposal names):
- GET /tenants/{tenant}/requests/{request_id}/playback -> list of events (paginated)
- POST /tenants/{tenant}/requests/{request_id}/playback/export -> returns presigned URL to signed evidence bundle
- GET /tenants/{tenant}/playback-manifest/{manifest_id} -> metadata about exported bundle

Security and privacy:
- Audit store obeys tenant retention settings; evidence exports can be suppressed for customers opting out of retention evidence for PII-laden flows (legal+sales to define opt-out policy).
- Evidence bundles redact token-level content unless tenant config explicitly enables full payload export. Redaction rules configurable by tenant.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Data model & schema aligned with ENG and SRE (2 sprints): event envelope, storage layout, signing model.
2) Runtime instrumentation (ENG) to write decision events at router/policy-engine and storage assignment (3 sprints). Events published to audit-store topic.
3) Audit store service (infra) that ingests, compacts, and exposes index by request_id (2 sprints).
4) API + export generation and signing (security + infra) (2 sprints).
5) Console UI and export UX (DX + PM) (2 sprints).
6) Alpha with 2 pilot tenants and targeted QA (3 weeks).

Rollout and gating:
- Feature flag per-tenant: residency_playback_v1. Default off.
- Pilot tenants: two legal/regulatory customers who have signed NDA for early access.
- Gate criteria: signed audit bundles validated by security (KMS chain), retrieval SLA met in staging, and no meaningful increase in request path latency.

Metrics to monitor:
- Playback event ingestion success rate
- Median size of export bundles
- Export generation latency
- Retrieval latency for GET playback API
- Number of requests with missing decision events

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Q1: What is the canonical list of reason_codes and do we map them to SOC 2 control IDs? (Need security/legal input)
- Q2: Should we include model logits/hash fingerprints in evidence? This could create privacy risk. (Eng + Legal)
- Q3: Retention defaults for audit store vs tenant-configured (cost tradeoff).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Audit store growth is large under high-traffic tenants. Mitigation: compaction policy, TTL defaults, and opt-in for deep recording.
- Risk: Evidence bundles contain PII. Mitigation: strict redaction by default + tenant config and legal review.

Artifacts and links:
- Design spec (confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMPLIANCE/pages/Residency+Playback+Design
- Proposed schema PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6821
- Prototype UI mockups: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ResidencyUiMockups

Next steps: schedule joint scoping with ENG/SRE/Security to finalize schema and signing model (target meeting week of 2025-03-31). Assign ENG tech lead and open ENG-82321 to track runtime instrumentation.
